title: Soft-fence passive extraction and atomic restore validation playbook
creator: Marcus Rivera
description:
Goal: Produce an operational playbook that validates active->passive failover semantics using a 'soft-fence' containment strategy, and exercise atomic snapshot restore across the tokenstore and KV layers with SLO gating. This ticket consolidates runbook steps, validation harnesses, acceptance criteria, and scheduled drill plans for a team-run failover rehearsal without full public traffic cutover.

Background: We've run multiple passive promotion rehearsals, but recent incidents show gaps in state divergence detection and subtle latency regressions after warm-standby promotion. The soft-fence approach aims to extract a subset of traffic and state (read-only traffic plus low-risk writes) into the passive region behind a fence, validate snapshot/restore fidelity and then progressively widen the fence if validations pass. This reduces blast radius while allowing us to test restore and rollback paths end-to-end.

Scope: tokenstore snapshot/restore, KV prefix reconcile, router-circuit behavior, autoscaler and batcher response to partial load, circuit-breaker thresholds, and dashboard SLO gating (p99 latency, 99.9% availability for control plane). Does NOT include full customer-visible DNS cutover.

Outcomes: A documented runbook stored in Confluence, an automation script in infra/tools to perform fenced extraction and restore, a small canary traffic harness, post-drill audit artifacts and a remediation checklist to close identified gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence runbook describing soft-fence choreography, operator commands, and rollback steps published and peer-reviewed
Automated snapshot/restore script (infra/tools/soft_fence_restore) able to restore tokenstore and KV prefixes to a staging passive cluster within target RTO < 10 minutes for 50GB state
Canary harness (github.com/redwood-inference/dr-drills/tree/soft-fence) validated end-to-end traffic path for read-only queries and low-risk writes and shows no data divergence after restore
Dashboard SLO gate triggers based on synthetic traffic (p99 latency < 200ms, error rate < 0.2%) and will abort widening fence if breached
Post-drill audit with snapshot checksums, KV prefix compare report, and a blameless incident memo created within 48 hours
preconditions: Dedicated staging passive region available and isolated from prod routing
Latest tokenstore snapshot completed and available in s3://redwood-dr-snapshots/<date>/
Owners for networking, infra, runtime, and on-call assigned for drill day
Security sign-off for KMS keys and snapshot access (ticket: SEC-2026-14)
runbook_steps: Step 0 - Pre-drill: Run dry-run of snapshot export and restore on dev cluster. Verify checksum match and record wall-clock times.

Step 1 - Fence creation: Apply routing policy that siphons 5% read traffic and routes low-risk write clients (internal SDK test keys) to passive region behind 'soft-fence' header. Monitor A/B router metrics.
Step 2 - Snapshot restore: Use infra/tools/soft_fence_restore to restore tokenstore snapshot and KV prefix set 'soft-fence-2026-03-12' into passive cluster. Validate no partial writes were lost.
Step 3 - State reconcile: Run kv-compare tool (sha256 checksums per prefix) and reconciliation script. If mismatch > 0.1% keys, abort widening fence and run diagnostic capture.
Step 4 - Behavioral tests: Run end-to-end canary suite (10k synthetic requests over 10 minutes) asserting output consistency, latency, and cache hit ratio. Monitor circuit-breaker trip counts.
Step 5 - SLO Gate: If p99 latency < 200ms and error rate < 0.2% for 15m, widen fence to 20% traffic. Otherwise, immediately rollback to fenced state and create incident ticket.
Step 6 - Wide validation: Repeat Step 4 for widened fence. If okay, escalate plan to schedule DNS-level cutover (outside scope of this ticket).
Rollback: Clear fencing policy and redirect traffic to primary; restore primary KV read replicas from latest snapshot if needed. Document exact commands and time-to-restore metrics.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Snapshot corruption mid-export. Mitigation: Verify checksums and keep last 3 snapshots; test restore on dev prior to drill.
Risk: Circuit-breaker floods on primary when fence widens. Mitigation: Use gradual widening (5% -> 20%) and enable extra shedding thresholds during drill window.
Risk: Operator error during restore. Mitigation: Two-person approval gate in runbook and automation to reduce manual steps.
Risk: KMS or IAM blocking restore. Mitigation: Pre-run IAM smoke test and temporary role delegation for drill; security to pre-approve keys.

decisions: Adopt soft-fence widening strategy rather than immediate full cutover to allow progressive validation and rollback.
Use checksum-based kv-compare for atomicity assertions rather than application-level reconciliation to catch low-level corruption.
Two-operator approval required at snapshot restore start and prior to any fence widening.
Circuit-breaker thresholds will be relaxed for synthetic canary traffic only; production thresholds unchanged.
